study_identification.title: Towards Longitudinal Characterization of Multiple Sclerosis Atrophy Employing SynthSeg Framework and Normative Modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: Investigate deviations in subcortical brain volumes of MS patients by comparing SynthSeg-derived morphometry to a large-scale normative model, aiming to support longitudinal characterization of disease progression.
study_characteristics.study_design_other: Pilot deviance analysis per time-point relative to a longitudinal normative trajectory; longitudinal acquisition in patients not clearly described in accessible text.

clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: MS patients exhibit significant deviations in subcortical volumes relative to a large normative model; integrating SynthSeg-based segmentation with normative modeling may improve characterization of MS progression.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI segmented with SynthSeg+ and SynthSeg-WMH, subcortical morphometric deviations were identified in 326 MS patients when compared to a reference normative model trained on 37,407 healthy individuals, suggesting potential for refined longitudinal progression modeling.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Details on normative model algorithm, predictors, dataset composition, quality control, and site/scanner handling were not available in the accessible text, limiting assessment of robustness and generalizability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Leverages DL-based segmentation (SynthSeg+, SynthSeg-WMH) to enable robust subcortical volume estimation in presence of WML and applies normative modeling for patient-specific deviation quantification.

general_notes.general_notes: Reference list cites normative modeling framework (Rutherford 2022) and Brain Charts for People Living with MS (Keshavan 2023), but the specific normative model implementation and datasets are not identified.
